q: Wang's tiling problem (deciding whether a finite set of Wang tiles tiles the plane) was proved undecidable by Berger (1966). The connection to dynamical systems is:
opts: Tilings are periodic orbits of cellular automata
A Wang tile set defines a 2D subshift; the emptiness problem for 2D SFTs is Π₁⁰-complete; 2D SFTs can simulate Turing machines
Every Wang tile set is an SFT in 1D
The tiling problem reduces to computing topological entropy
exp: Wang tiles define 2D subshifts X_τ. Whether X_τ is nonempty (tiles exist) is Π₁⁰-complete because finding a valid tiling requires checking all finite configurations — you can never confirm non-existence computably. Turing machine simulation shows undecidability.
